name: Ha Giang food guide
summary: Ha Giang eats from the highland pot: thắng cố at the Sunday market, mèn mén steamed from stone-milled corn, cháo ấu tẩu against the cold, and buckwheat in cakes, noodles, and wine. Breakfast in town is phở, and in Đồng Văn it is bánh cuốn in hot broth.
body: Plan your meals around Sunday, when the markets in Đồng Văn and Mèo Vạc fill up and a thắng cố stall feeds the traders. Buckwheat foods belong to the flower season, and the Đồng Văn buckwheat festival is typically mid-to-late November.
The same name can arrive as a different pot from one kitchen to the next. Thắng cố comes with horse, buffalo, beef, or pork, and cháo ấu tẩu with sticky rice and pork hock or with minced meat.
specialtiesLead: The highland dishes to know by name, plus phở at breakfast.

sections.heading: Ha Giang specialties
paragraphs: Buckwheat turns up as a cake, pancakes, porridge, noodles, vermicelli, pho, beer, and wine, and each is its own dish. Corn does the same work in mèn mén, grilled corn cakes, corn pho, and corn wine.

spots.name: Five-colour sticky rice
spots.note: Sticky rice dyed with forest leaves in five colours for the five elements: yellow earth, green plant, red fire, white metal, and black water. It is eaten across the northern uplands as well as in Đồng Văn.

spots.name: Buckwheat cake
spots.note: Buckwheat seed ground to powder, mixed with water, poured into a soft mould, and rolled into a cake you will not mistake for any other. Look for it in buckwheat-flower season and at the November festival.

spots.name: Buckwheat pancakes
spots.note: Buckwheat pancakes are a festival food in Đồng Văn, served beside the buckwheat porridge, noodles, cakes, and wine. They are a separate dish from the bánh tam giác mạch cake.

spots.name: Buckwheat porridge
spots.note: A porridge of buckwheat on the festival table in Đồng Văn, typically mid-to-late November.

spots.name: Buckwheat noodles
spots.note: Noodles made from buckwheat seed, eaten on the plateau and at the November festival.

spots.name: Buckwheat dry rice vermicelli
spots.note: A dry vermicelli from the plateau’s buckwheat kitchen, made with buckwheat seed.

spots.name: Buckwheat pho
spots.note: A pho made with buckwheat seed, its own bowl apart from the breakfast phở and phở Tráng Kìm.

spots.name: Buckwheat beer
spots.note: Beer made from buckwheat seed, one of the drinks of the plateau’s buckwheat harvest.

spots.name: Buckwheat wine
spots.note: Wine made from buckwheat, poured with the buckwheat foods and at the Đồng Văn festival. It is a different drink from the corn wine.

spots.name: Leaf-fermented corn wine
spots.note: Leaf-fermented corn wine is the drink with thắng cố and the shot a host may pour for a guest. Lợn cắp nách comes with rượu ngô or with rượu táo mèo.

spots.name: Grilled stone moss
spots.note: Grilled stone moss is one of the Hà Giang highland dishes, eaten on the plateau.

spots.name: Hunchback chung cake
spots.note: A palm-sized Red Dao chưng cake with a hunched back, shaped like a woman carrying a basket: upland sticky rice, mung beans, and black or fatty pork wrapped in dong or galangal leaves. It boils 8–10 hours over a wood stove and comes out soft, chewy, and fragrant.

spots.name: Sausages
spots.note: Sausages are among the highland meats of Hà Giang, apart from the smoked lạp xưởng gác bếp.

spots.name: Lap xuong gac bep
spots.note: Đồng Văn sausage of thịt lợn mán in a casing of small intestine, seasoned with mắc mật, mắc khén, white rice wine, and ginger, then hung over the kitchen fire. It comes out smoky, fatty, and fragrant, and travelers buy it to carry home.

spots.name: Thang co
spots.note: The Hmong market-day pot of horse, buffalo, beef, or pork with the bones and offal, simmered with spices such as star anise, cardamom, cinnamon, and thảo quả, though some cooks leave the spices out to keep the meat’s own fragrance. Eat it from the pot on a cold day with mèn mén, grilled corn cakes, corn wine, or green vegetables.

spots.name: Men men
spots.note: Hmong cornmeal: dried corn milled on stone, sieved, moistened, and steamed twice, eaten with thắng cố or on its own. Chew it slowly for a nutty, sweet, rich taste.

spots.name: Grilled corn cakes
spots.note: Corn cakes off the grill, eaten with thắng cố and corn wine.

spots.name: Au tau porridge
spots.note: Rice porridge cooked with the ấu tẩu tuber, soaked in rice water and simmered for hours, with sticky rice and pork hock or minced meat. It tastes bitter first and sweet after, and comes hot with scallion, herbs, and pepper on cold days.

spots.name: Dong Van steamed rice rolls
spots.note: Thin steamed rice rolls of minced pork and wood-ear mushroom, served Tày style in a bowl of hot bone broth rather than with a cold dipping sauce. Some breakfast bowls on Phố Cổ add egg, chives, and chả.

spots.name: Dong Van egg steamed rice rolls
spots.note: A Đồng Văn rice roll made with egg, sold as its own dish beside the plain steamed rolls.

spots.name: Bac Me bamboo-tube rice
spots.note: Rice cooked in bamboo tubes, a specialty of Bắc Mê on the road back toward Hà Giang town. The district is also known for Bắc Mê sticky rice.

spots.name: Dried buffalo meat
spots.note: Black Thái buffalo dried in the kitchen smoke and served to guests, numbing and hot from mắc khén and sweet from the meat. Buy it at Đồng Văn market or from a household to carry home.

spots.name: Sour pho
spots.note: A sour pho of the plateau, a separate bowl from the breakfast phở and phở Tráng Kìm.

spots.name: Corn pho
spots.note: A corn pho of the plateau, a separate bowl from buckwheat pho.

spots.name: Pho Trang Kim
spots.note: A handmade Đồng Văn phở of thick, chewy noodles in a light, sweet broth with firm chicken.

spots.name: Thang den
spots.note: Round sticky-rice balls filled with crushed mung beans, boiled and served hot with coconut milk and ginger, sweet and slightly rich. Think of Hanoi’s floating cakes, not thắng cố.

spots.name: Thit treo
spots.note: Thịt treo, hanging meat, is one of the province’s highland specialties.

spots.name: Lon cap nach
spots.note: Small free-range pigs of 4 to 10 kg, carried to market under the arm and raised on corn, cassava, roots, and forest greens. The meat is roasted whole, grilled in bamboo, or steamed and dipped in salt pounded with green chili and mắc khén, with crisp skin, little fat, and firm lean meat.

spots.name: Shan tuyet tea
spots.note: Tea from old Shan tuyết trees, one of the province’s highland specialties.

spots.name: Mint honey
spots.note: Mint honey is one of the plateau tastes to try on the loop.

spots.name: Black chicken hotpot
spots.note: A Đồng Văn hotpot of black chicken with white radish, mushroom, cải mèo, peas, and forest greens. The free-range bird is firm, fragrant, and naturally sweet.

spots.name: Stone cake
spots.note: Dao and Nùng stone cake, also called bánh Lơ khoải, of rice, corn, and sticky rice, yellow or purple, left in a stream for months until moss grows, then scraped and cut into finger-wide strips. Eat it in place of noodles, as a cool bite, or boiled soft with palm sugar and roasted peanuts, especially at Tết and Dao festivals.

sections.heading: Markets and stalls
paragraphs: Sunday is market day in Đồng Văn and Mèo Vạc, and your host will know when the stalls fill. Phố Cáo meets once a week, Tam Sơn feeds the first day’s lunch, and Bắc Mê is the stall stop on the way down.

spots.name: Dong Van market
spots.note: The old-quarter market, busiest on Sunday, with trading at night or in the early morning. Ask your host when to go.

spots.name: Meo Vac market
spots.note: A Sunday market where a thắng cố stall feeds the traders.

spots.name: Pho Cao market
spots.note: A weekly market for household goods, clothes, and spices, with Flower Hmong skirts and Black Hmong tunics. Ask your host which day it meets.

spots.name: Tam Son stalls
spots.note: The first-day lunch stop in xã Quản Bạ, where road stalls and restaurants serve northern food and coffee is easy to find.

spots.name: Bac Me stalls
spots.note: Local food stalls on QL34 along the Gâm, the stop on the last morning.

sections.heading: Breakfast
paragraphs: In town, the morning of the second day is phở, before the ride toward Đồng Văn. In Đồng Văn, breakfast is bánh cuốn on Phố Cổ.

spots.name: Pho Co
spots.note: Bánh cuốn in the morning, filled with pork and wood ear and served in hot broth, with egg, chives, and chả at some tables.

seoTitle: Ha Giang food — thang co, au tau, and breakfast pho
seoDescription: What to eat on the Ha Giang Loop: thắng cố, cháo ấu tẩu, mèn mén, buckwheat cakes and wine, smoked buffalo, and Sunday markets in Đồng Văn and Mèo Vạc.
